title: Ordered Tree

story.briefing: This lattice is ordered. Knowing that, you should never have to look at more than a handful of junctions to answer whether a value is present.
story.success: Lookup confirmed in a handful of steps. The ordered lattice proves its worth.

description: A binary search tree holds, at every node, only smaller values in its left subtree and only larger values in its right. All values are distinct. Given such a tree and a target, return true if the target appears in it and false otherwise. Do not examine more of the tree than you need to. A tree is given as an array where the node at index i has its left child at index 2i+1 and its right child at index 2i+2. A null entry means there is no node there, and nothing exists beneath it. An empty array is an empty tree.
hints: Comparing the target against a node value tells you which single subtree could possibly contain it. The other subtree can be ignored entirely.
This is binary search wearing a different costume. Scanning every node also gives the right answer, which is exactly why it is worth checking that you did not.
Start at the root. If the value matches, return true. If the target is smaller go left, otherwise go right. Return false when you run off the tree.
